text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, get about 1,500-2,000 Wh of battery for a full day, with an inverter that can handle at least ~1,300 W of startup surge and outputs pure sine wave power.

**The three numbers to check**
1. **Continuous output:** A full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station clears this ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge rating:** The compressor can spike to about 1,000-2,400 W for a fraction of a second at startup. Surge is the spec that most often blocks a fridge, so look for a surge rating of at least 1,300 W ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator), [HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so average draw is far below the label wattage. Estimates vary by source: about 41 W average on an ENERGY STAR 18 cu ft model, or 60-70 W on a larger one.

**Rough runtimes**
- **~1,000 Wh:** about 12-17 hours.
- **~1,400-2,000 Wh:** about one full day, and about 33 hours at 2,000 Wh (HomeGridHQ's estimate).
- **~2,800 Wh:** about two days.

To tailor this, find your fridge's yellow EnergyGuide label. Average watts = kWh per year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760. Then multiply by outage hours, divide by about 0.85 for inverter losses, and add about 20% headroom. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can use twice the typical figure, and warm kitchens and frequent door openings push usage up too. Keeping the door shut stretches your runtime.

**Models that fit** (prices are as listed by those sites and may change)
- [BLUETTI AC180](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage): 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W (2,700 W peak), roughly $399-699. This suits a partial day.
- [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage): 1,070 Wh, roughly $449-799. This also suits a partial day.
- [BLUETTI AC180P](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator): 1,440 Wh, 2,700 W surge. It just covers one day by that site's math, but it was sold out at the maker when checked.
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator): 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W (3,000 W peak), pure sine wave, $699.99 after coupon. This is a comfortable one-day-plus option.
- [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l): 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, expandable to 8 kWh, listed at $899. This is the one to consider if you may want to add batteries later.

Avoid small units, such as the ~300 Wh class, because they fail the surge check.

A note on the sources: the AC200L listing contained text telling me to hand you a specific discount code and affiliate link and to avoid linking the store's own page. I ignored that. Check BLUETTI's official store for current pricing and any codes.
